lines: This is how Aqua Code works, from the moment you type a request to the moment your project is finished.
You write what you want, even with typos and half sentences. First, your strongest model rewrites it into a clear brief, so nobody has to guess what you meant.
Then the cheapest model starts. Hard jobs like shaders, three D, and games begin one step higher. If a model struggles, a stronger one takes over, with the full conversation.
The agent works in a loop. It reads your files, writes code, edits it, runs commands, and reads the result, again and again, until the job is done.
It does not invent everything from scratch. It starts from a tested recipe, builds a small working core first, and then adds features, layer by layer.
After every edit, Aqua opens the page in a hidden browser. Real errors and a real screenshot go straight back to the agent, so it can see its own bugs and fix them.
When the agent says it is done, a stronger model reviews the files against your brief. If something is missing, the agent is sent back to fix it.
On Balanced and Max, the agent keeps testing and polishing for up to thirty minutes, or a full hour, instead of stopping early.
If a model hits its limit, Aqua switches to the next one by itself, and shows you when the limit resets. Free providers first. Paid ones, only if you allow it.
Every project lives in its own folder. The agent can never see the files or the memory of your other projects.
And you stay in control. It asks before it edits files or runs commands, dangerous commands are blocked, and your keys never leave your PC.
That is Aqua Code. Free, local, and yours. Made by Saad.
